recipes.name: Baked Green Vegetables
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2 inch pieces

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish and set aside.

Fill a saucepan with water, bring to a boil over medium heat, and boil the Brussels sprouts and broccoli for 2 minutes, until thawed. Add the asparagus, and boil for 3 more minutes, until the vegetables are hot, lightly cooked, and bright green.

Drain the Brussels sprouts, broccoli, and asparagus, place into the prepared baking dish, and dot with butter. Stir to melt the butter, and mix in the spinach, garlic powder, black pepper, and bread crumbs.

Bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes to heat the vegetables, remove from the oven, and stir in the Cheddar cheese. Return to the oven, and bake for 20 minutes or until cheese is melted, spinach is cooked, and casserole is hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Green Vegetables
raw_recipe.description: Brussels sprouts, broccoli, asparagus, and spinach are baked with crumbs and cheese and served hot.

review.reviewBody: This is great! I added a few almond slivers and some parmesean cheese into the recipe and it was yummy. I'm new to cooking, so easy and delicious, I will definitely try this one again!

My daughter and I LOVED this dish! We even enjoyed the warmed up leftovers. I used all fresh vegetables and lessened the amount of Brussels sprouts after reading some of the other reviews. I steamed the broccoli and Brussels sprouts until just turning tender as directed but roasted the asparagus with 3 pieces of bacon on a baking sheet for 25 minutes rather than steaming them. I then tossed all the vegetables together with the bacon, crumbled, and a little bit of the bacon drippings. I sprinkled the bread crumbs on top (not as much as was called for) and at the end sprinkled the top with a little grated cheddar rather than mixing the cheese in. I am excited about making this dish for a large family gathering next week as I know it will be a hit. This is absolutely the best way to eat your green veggies!

Just found this recipe. it was a hit!! I used fresh veggies, asparagus, Brussel sprouts, and green beans. The asparagus was lost in the mix. Next time I will cut the sprouts in half. I added caramelized onions which I added the garlic to. I used smart balance to reduce cholesterol, and I used taco cheese which melted very well, I also used panko bread crumbs mixed in, only thing I had on hand. I had a lot of veggies so I made a big tray and froze half of the leftovers. Next time I will add bacon, or ground beef. Definitely marked as a favorite, its easy, quick and very changeable.

Family loved it. I did use all fresh vegetables. I did a short parboil of veggies and also added 1/2 Cup chopped onions, 1/4 Cup fresh garlic and a little more cheese (only had swiss). Turned out scrumptious. I'm making it again this week and will use the recipe as written.

Fresh vegetables are tastier and easy to use. I made this with many different veggies and a whole package of mushrooms following the advice to soften the Brussels sprouts, broccoli and eggplant before baking. As I didn’t have bread crumbs I used crushed Ak-Mak crackers. They worked great. I added spicy chicken sausage. My wife claims it was the best dish I’ve ever made.

Excellent! I used fresh vegetables as per the other suggestion and was very pleased with the results. Next time I'll cut the brussel sprouts in half after cooking them (my microwave has a vegetable cycle that makes this a snap) to distribute them better.
This Vegetable bake came out scrumptious. I didn't have broccoli, so I used fresh Brussel sprouts, asparagus and onions with fresh spinach. The family loved it. Always a plus.

I think the amount of bread crumbs was a little too much and probably should have been added at the end as they ended up being a bit soggy when it was all done. Also the cooking time was a little too long as the veggies ended up being a bit too mushy. I think if it cooked a little less, with a little bit more spice [of some kind], it would have been a bit more flavorful.

I'm giving this 5 stars because my kids asked me to make it again. They gobbled it down and wanted more. The kids and I don't really like Broccoli, Asparagus, Spinach, or Brussel Sprouts. But, we wanted to be healthy so we made this. We did use all FRESH, no frozen vegetables. We used extra cheese and breadcrumbs. We cooked it as long as the recipe said - it could have been ok cooked less but again, no complaints.

I'm just saying if you want to be healthy and eat those green veggies and you are tired of the same old salad, this is the way to go.

I used recipe as a guide because I had a ton of fresh spinach and asparagus to cook, and leftover fresh ground and seasoned bread crumbs. I did not use the brussels sprouts or broccoli, but would if I plan ahead in the future. I thought it was okay, something different, but my roommates loved it and kept picking at it before I could even put it away. I give it 4 stars because I did not follow it exactly and because of the compliments and snacking by my friends :)

Alot of flavors going on here with the various vegetables. The asparagus flavor is lost with the stronger flavors of the Brussels Sprouts and Broccoli. No reason to use frozen vegetables in this. Use fresh.

I cooked the veggies on the stove in EVOO because boiling causes veggies to lose their nutrients. I used 1/8 cup of oats instead of bread crumbs and I should have just left them out. I think this was only good because I cooked these in oil. I wouldn't have liked them steamed. I didn't have brussel sprouts so it was just a bag of broccoli and asparagus. Probably won't make them again.
I did not use Brussels sprouts, and I used frozen asparagus. It turned out very good. Next time I will add a little salt and maybe some dried ground chipotle peppers for added flavor.
Such an amazing dish and delightful flavor. Didn't have to add any additional season to it!! This one is definitely getting served at our table this Thanksgiving! Thank YOU for sharing it!!
Basic good idea, but too much cooking time. Also the brussel sprouts overpowered the other veggies. I will not make this again without serious modifications.
